messages:
kevin: Heads-up — since the 03:00 kernel rollout in us-west2 we're seeing ~30% of GPU pods stuck Pending with "no GPUs available".

maria: logs?

kevin: device-plugin container (nvidia-device-plugin) keeps spamming:
```
E0312 03:12:45.123456 kubelet_deviceplugin.go:150] Failed to allocate device: driver version mismatch (required >= 515.86, found 510.39)
```
Nodes show modinfo nvidia: 510.39 on some, 515.86 on others.

dina: did the kernel update also trigger DKMS rebuilds? maybe modules failed to compile on older kernels.

kevin: yes, some nodes ended up with a newer kernel (5.15.0-105) but DKMS compiled nvidia-515 only on nodes with headers present; others stayed on 510.39. kubelet reports GPU capacity then wrong.

julian: also seeing NCCL errors in training pods on those nodes:
```
NCCL WARN Call to cudaGetDeviceProperties failed: invalid device function
```
Suggests mismatch between driver and CUDA runtime.

maria: what's the GPU operator version? we recently upgraded to gpu-operator 2.6.1 in staging, and 2.6.2 in prod this morning.

kevin: yep 2.6.2. It introduced devicePluginPreStart changes and a strict driver-check probe. Pods that previously tolerated mismatch now get blocked.

dina: can we quickly taint problematic nodes and drain them? we need to avoid scheduling until drivers are consistent.

kevin: I'm tainting us-west2-nodeset-b: kubectl taint nodes -l gw=us-west2 problem=gpu-driver:NoSchedule
Done.

maria: opened Nvidia ticket with logs and kernel list. Also creating a rollback PR to pin gpu-operator to 2.6.1 for prod.

oncall: we should run a node-level fixscript to rebuild DKMS modules where headers present. proposing rolling script:
```
ssh node-$i 'apt-get install linux-headers-$(uname -r) && dkms autoinstall && systemctl restart kubelet'
```
run 10 nodes/hour.

julian: also add an admission webhook to block pods requesting cuda-12 if driver <515.

kevin: short-term plan: 1) taint/drain affected nodes 2) run dkms rebuild script (ops) 3) rollback gpu-operator to 2.6.1 if rebuilds don't succeed 4) schedule maintenance window for 03:00 UTC next weekend to standardize kernel+driver images.

maria: cost note — draining nodes into spare capacity will push workloads to Dedicated burst pool. estimated extra $2k/day if we keep bursts for 48h. flagging for finance.

dina: will also add a preflight check in infra-bootstrap to verify nvidia-driver>= required before untaint.

kevin: putting runbook in incidents board. tags: @infra, @platform.

infra-bot: Incident created: INF-2026-0423 - GPU driver mismatch after kernel rollout — link https://redwood.tools/incidents/INF-2026-0423

maria: thanks, assigning to @dina for ops and @kevin for rollout coordination.

kevin: I'll follow up in #eng-sre once we have consistent node list.

dina: starting first batch now (nodes 1-10) — will post status updates.

kevin: update 03:45 — first batch succeeded on 8/10 nodes (2 failed due to missing headers). continuing.
